page: Microsoft Azure E8-2ds_v6 is an Edsv6-family virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8573C core. Operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this instance features Hyper-Threading with 2 threads per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. Local storage is provided via a bundled 472 GB NVMe SSD.

Benchmark data reveals a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core performance. The instance achieves strong single-core metrics, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2156.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression performance at 31.32 GB/sec. However, due to its low core count of 1 physical core, multi-core performance is limited, as evidenced by a poor stress-ng multi-core score of 1991.98 and a weak Geekbench multi-core score of 2649.0. Memory bandwidth also shows constraints under large block sizes, with uncached read and write speeds falling into the poor category at 21.49 GB/sec and 14.14 GB/sec respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E8-2ds_v6 offers high memory density relative to its compute footprint, making it suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require massive parallel processing. The inclusion of a local NVMe SSD provides fast temporary storage. This hardware profile is best suited for workloads such as small-scale in-memory databases, caching layers, lightweight text processing, or single-threaded applications requiring a large memory footprint but minimal CPU concurrency.
